### What cycle 20 changes (`ddb0ba1`, `f066083`, `bf1d4eb`, `daa426d`)

- **The drain's visits after verdicts share one turn's ids** (item 1). `EngineState.drainIDsLeft` holds what the
  drain's turn has left. At the follow's end the drain runs in the follow's last turn, so that turn seeds it with what
  its visits left (`drainEventsAfterFollow(ids: budget.ids)`); a drain follow-up turn seeds it with a whole turn's
  (`followIDsPerTurn`). `followAfterVerdict` visits within what is left, and subtracts what it moved. When nothing is
  left, or a visit left a rest (`followMoving`, cycle 19), the rest of the batch goes back to the head of
  `eventsAfterFollow` with its stamps, in order, for the next drain turn. The events keep their order, so no answer
  changes (S3-R20 item 3).
- **A job's lane is read from per-lane interest counts** (item 2). `Job.interests` is `private(set)`, and only `Job`'s
  mutators change it: `setInterest`, `insertAsset`, `removeAsset`, `subtractAssets`, `setAssets`,
  `removeAllInterests` and `keepInterests`. `setInterest`, `removeAllInterests` and `keepInterests` keep
  `Job.interestCounts` (`InterestCounts`): bulk, prefetch, user-initiated, and the user-initiated interests that are
  not `.ensure`, which `isSingleUser` reads.
  - `Job.lane` is `interestCounts.highest ?? heldLane ?? .bulk`.
  - `dropInterest` changes the job in place, with no copy of it alive across the removal. A copy shares the storage of
    its interests, so the removal used to copy them whole.
  - A retry verdict's answer for each interest (`verdictAnswers` in `EngineFailures`) reads the lane `retryLater`
    reads: the job's, less the interests the count answers. That lane is now `interestCounts.highest {
    !reachesCap($0, attempts:) }`. Before, it walked the job's interests for each interest read, O(interests²) a
    verdict; the inventory found it (item 3).
  - The new invariant: each job's counts equal a recount of its interests.
- **No follow starts once the engine stops running** (item 7). The unknown-id admission (`EngineManifest`) now
  re-reads the lifecycle after `planningView()`, its last await. Once shutdown began it returns before
  `followStoreView` and `noteBound`; until now it re-read the lifecycle only after them. An apply's end and a catch-up
  already re-read it first. `scheduleFollowFollowUp` spawns its task without checking the result, and
  `followBarrierViolations` reports `a follow is owed while the engine is <lifecycle>`.
- **The seam `EngineState.admissionsForTests`** (item 4). It is `nil` by default. A test sets it to `[]` and reads each
  admission (`AttemptAdmission`: transfer, ticket, queue place, attempt) in the engine's order. No production path sets
  it.

### Removals (S3-R19 item 3; S3-R24 item 3)

- **`scheduleFollowFollowUp`'s unspawnable branch** (`bf1d4eb`). It ran when `spawn` refused the follow-up task, which
  `spawn` does only while the engine is shutting down or degraded. The branch reset `followFollowUpScheduled`,
  `followOrder` and `followNext`, `followScans`, `followCarried` and `pumpWaitsForFollow`, and called
  `releaseInboundWaits`, which drops `followMoving` and the owed moves and resumes the publications that waited. Why
  nothing is lost without it:
  - A follow starts only while the engine runs. An apply's end and a catch-up re-read the lifecycle before they
    follow, and since `bf1d4eb` so does the unknown-id admission, the one path that did not
    (`admissionStraddlingShutdownFollowsNothing`).
  - The engine degrades only while starting, before any apply, so no follow is owed then.
  - Shutdown's first turn and the drain after each task it joins (`drainEverything`) drop the job table and redo
    every reset but one: `followOrder`, `followNext`, `followScans`, `followCarried`, `pumpWaitsForFollow` and
    `releaseInboundWaits`.
  - The exception, `followFollowUpScheduled`, needs no reset. A follow-up already scheduled clears the flag, finds the
    engine shutting down and returns at once (`followFollowUp`), and while shutting down nothing new is spawned to wait
    on the flag.
  - `followBarrierViolations` checks the assumption (`!isRunning && followOwed`). The test forces it by setting
    `followOrder = [b]` on the shut-down engine, and reads the one violation.

  `scheduleDrainFollowUp` has an analogous `spawned == nil` branch (`EngineFollow.swift:390`), which this cycle does not
  change. It has 0 hits (under "Not reached and structural lines (cycle 20)").

### Test changes (G3 one-to-one; S3-R16 item 4)

1. `EngineFollowBarrierReplayTests.swift`, `barrierReadmitsBehindTheOwedVisitsPlaces` (`daa426d`; item 4).

     re-queues (visit-first): …")`.
   - New: `#expect(admitted.first?.transfer == n.transferID, "N, queued at P's visit, is admitted before the members
     the follow-up re-queues (visit-first): …")`, where `admitted` is the engine's admissions
     (`admissionsForTests = []` is set before the apply), plus `#expect(Set(admitted.map(\.transfer)) ==
     others.union([n.transferID]), …)`.
   - The assertion on the set of starts is unchanged, and so are the tuning, the scenario and the doc comment's
     premise. The comment now says why the order is the engine's.
2. `EngineFollowBarrierVerdictAnswersTests.swift` (`f066083`, `431d397`).
   - `job.interests[token] = interests[token]` (`:55`) becomes `job.setInterest(interests[token], for: token)`.
   - The three `job.interests[x] = JobInterest(…)` lines (`:154-156` on `49a0493`) become
     `job.setInterest(JobInterest(…), for: x)`, with the same values. The property is `private(set)` now, and the
     mutator keeps the counts.

3. `EngineRegressionCycle16Tests.swift:472`: `job.interests[InterestToken(rawValue: 1)] = JobInterest(…)` becomes
   `job.setInterest(JobInterest(…), for: InterestToken(rawValue: 1))`, with the same interest.

   `state.jobs[…]?.removeAllInterests()`.
5. `EngineOutcomeTests.swift`, `invariantOracle`: the orphaned case's `interests.removeAll()` becomes
   `removeAllInterests()`, and a `miscounted` expectation is added for the counts clause.
6. BenchSync's `concentrationPublicationTurns` (`c03c0e8`; S3-R24 item 2). The case now goes on through the commit:
   `concentrationTurns(.publication, label:)` becomes `concentrationTurns(.publication, commit: .bound, label:)`, and
   its display name says "begins and commits". The wait it checks spans both the publication's start and its commit,
   so the old check is kept and extended.

None of these removes or weakens an assertion. The mutator changes write the same interests through the API that
keeps their counts.

### Mutants (S3-R16 1(e); S3-R25 items 1, 2, 5 to 8 and 10)

The runner is `.build-s3f/c20/mut.py`. It works on a copy of `Sources` and `Tests` (`.build-s3f/mutsrc`) built in
`.build-s3f/mutbuild`, never in place. Each mutant runs its filter twice. A mutant that survives its filter also runs
the whole Sync bundle (`full1`, then `full2`). Every round ends with the copy reverted, and `diff -r` against the
worktree's `Sources` was empty. Round 1's diff showed one line, the admission record (`daa426d`): it was written in
the worktree while that round ran, after the copy had been made.

Equivalent (`moveInterestGoneDrop`).

- **`moveInterestGoneDrop` is Equivalent** (S3-R19 item 2). With the token's interest gone, the mutant reads a
  stand-in interest and goes on to `:205`. There `removeAsset(asset, for: token)` finds no interest under the token,
  returns `false`, and the item is skipped. That is exactly what `:203`'s `continue` does, so no decision, answer or
  state differs. `:203` is still reached: `moveInterestGoneReroute` drops both guards, re-routes the gone interest, and
  is killed 2/2 at `:213`. The two guards stay, as item 8 says, and `:205`'s removal is what decides once the
  interest is gone.

`followIDsPerTurn` (512); N is a job's ids, I a job's interests, E the events waiting. The reference set is 10,000 ids,
however their interests are grouped (item 2). The figures are the gate run's (under "Gate evidence (cycle 20)") unless
a commit is named. A figure marked "(cycle 21's gate run)" is from the first gate run's release benchmarks ("Gate
evidence (cycle 21)", "The first run"), on `2c351e8`, whose `Sources` the final HEAD keeps, best of 3; a best above
8.5 ms is "at the edge" (S3-R26 item 9). The second run's, on `e599ae1`, are listed there: 51 of 53 are higher, by a
median of 3.3 %, and the one status they change, `purgeWhileOwedTurns`', is noted in its row.

### A holder re-created between turns (correct #4; S3-R25 item 9)

- **The case.** `continueMove` re-reads its holder by `TransferID`, which is derived from content. A job removed
  between two turns of its move and created again for the same content is found under the same key. The moves left
  (`MoveProgress`'s (id, token) items) then name the old job's interests.
- **Why the per-interest guards make the stale items no-ops.**
  - Tokens come from a counter (`EngineLifecycle`, `lastToken`), one per registration, so the re-created job holds an
    interest under an item's token only if that same registration's interest came back onto the content. An item
    whose token is not there is skipped at `:202-203`. One whose interest no longer holds the id is skipped at
    `:205-206`.
  - An item passes both guards only if the re-created holder holds that same interest in that same id. Then `reroute`
    moves it under the current copy, as the re-created job's own visit would. If the copy maps the id to this content
    again, `reroute` re-joins it here (`addInterest`), so the job keeps it.
  - Behind the barrier no join adds a new interest in an id of the rest: every join but the follow's own waits
    (`addInterest`'s `.join` events), and the drain that replays them waits until the rest is done (`followOwed`
    covers `followMoving`). So the interests in a rest's id are its items' tokens until the rest moves the id.
  - No holder epoch is added (S3-R25 item 9).
- **An observation, not probed.** `continueMove` removes the id from the holder's ids (`Job.assets`, `:195`) at the
  item's first interest, before the guards. The removal can matter in only one state: the holder holds the id under a
  token that is not among its items, and every item of the id is stale. That needs the same id on two jobs at once
  (a publishing job's id can be, as in the checksum-less test). It also needs that job's visit, under a later apply,
  to move the id's interest onto the re-created holder, and every item's interest to have left meanwhile. No path
  that builds this was found, and none was tried. It is put to the orchestrator with that shape.

### Open (blocking; not fixed this cycle)

1. **RR-21's two misses** (S3-R24 item 2; S3-R22 item 1), at a quiet load, best of 3:
   - The commit's re-routes: `committed` re-routes, in one turn, every interest in an id the publication does not
     bind because an apply moved it away. That was 48.47 ms best for 10,000 ids, at a 1-minute load of 2.73 to 2.99.
   - The drain's take-off: `replayVerdict` takes a job's moved-before ids off before its verdict
     (`takeOffMovedBefore`) and re-routes them after it (`rerouteMovedBefore`), each in one turn. That was 45.51 ms
     best for 10,000 ids, at a 1-minute load of 1.90 to 1.94.
   - The gate run on `c03c0e8` measured 48.68 and 45.67 ms best, at a 1-minute load of 2.21 to 5.59 (under "Gate
     evidence (cycle 20)").

   The fix was not attempted this cycle. Both re-routes must keep the visit-first answers while they span turns
   (S3-R20 item 3), and the state they would leave between turns needs its own invariants. The proposed design, put
   to the orchestrator:
   - **Turn the owed re-routes into drain events.** A `.reroutes(batch)` event carries the (token, id) pairs and the
     copy that found them, and is queued where the re-routes are made now. Each drain turn spends at most
     `drainIDsLeft` of them.
   - **Keep a limbo index.** It records the interests taken off a job and not yet re-routed, so the invariants (a
     waiter's interest, a group's members, the run's claims) accept them while they are owed. `followedLane` counts
     them by the rule of the job they left, as it does for an owed move's ids.
   - **Hold a publication while re-routes are owed.** `inboundBlocks` makes a publication wait while re-routes onto
     or off its job are owed, as it does for the owed moves.
   - **Decide each re-route under its event's copy.** The decision T21 reads is made under the copy the event
     carries, and the join under the copy current at the re-route.
   - **Clear and seam them like the owed moves.** Shutdown drops them, and the seam `rerouteIDsPerTurn` lets a test
     count them per turn.
   - **Extend the same treatment to the O(N) `supersede` row** of the inventory.

   The pins would be S3-R23 item 3's two: a deterministic per-turn count with the bound's drop-mutant, and the two
   BenchSync cases above, best of 3, at most `c2Budget`.
2. **`waitingTarget`'s `queued`, `blocked` and `downloading` case** (reqs #3; S3-R24 item 3). Not reached by a test,
   not removed, and not shown Equivalent:
   - `downloading` at the move's epoch cannot happen. A move is recorded at its target's attempt end, and only a new
     attempt's start makes the job download again, and that start gives it a new epoch (`Job.epoch`).
   - `blocked` at the move's epoch comes only after the `queued` case below. A job leaves its attempt's end for
     `blocked` only through a park. The parks that act on a job at its attempt's end are verdicts, and they wait in
     the drain while a move is owed. A queued job's parks (the admission gate, a space sweep) need the `queued` case
     first.
   - `queued` at the move's epoch happens on one path: the ENOENT re-queue of a drained publication
     (`publicationFailed`, `.fileSystem(.notFound)` with `cancelledAttempt`). That re-queue also happens behind the
     barrier, and the job keeps its epoch until its next start, which the barrier holds back. In that window,
     `continueInbound` drops the move (`waitingTarget` is `nil`), and the holder's own visit later moves the id. On a
     visit-first engine, the id would already be on the target, so the difference is only the job the id waits on
     until the visit, and its place and ticket. By the reading of `followedLane`, the id counts by its holder's rule
     there (`carried` is `nil`), the rule its holder's visit moves it by, and the queued target has no verdict waiting
     to differ.

   This is a reading of the code. No test builds the window this cycle (a drained attempt's publication failing with
   ENOENT while a move onto its job is owed and the follow's turns are held), so it is neither Reached nor proven
   Equivalent: in `continueInbound` the case changes order and tickets, so it is not Equivalent under S3-R19 item 2's
   "no state" either. Put to the orchestrator: reach it with that shape (the fakes can fail a publication with ENOENT
   after a cancelled attempt's staging, as `EngineRaceTests` does) and kill its drop-mutant, or rule the
   order-and-ticket difference a residual risk (S3-R16 item 2).

   **Corrected in cycle 21** (S3-R26 item 5; `analyse-g4-reach.md` (b) and (c)). The `queued` claim above is false:
   the ENOENT re-queue is not the only path to `queued` at a move's epoch. `relane`'s failed arm re-queues a failed
   job for a user interest (T20) with no start, so with no new epoch, and an ENOSPC's exit sets its job failed before
   its free-space read, whose turn runs one follow turn behind the barrier (`advanceFollowForSpaceSweep`): a join that
   turn makes onto the job re-queued it. Cycle 21 keeps the follow's visits that stand for an apply made before the end
   from re-queueing (probe (i), for a publication's ENOSPC and for a transfer's), but a visit for an apply made during
   the read still re-queues the job, as a visit-first engine's visit then met it failed. The `blocked` claim holds only
   while the barrier stays up: in that window the follow and its drain can end during the read, the drain's pump can
   dispatch the re-queued job, and the gate can park it at the same epoch (UNCONFIRMED there, from the code; not probed
   in cycle 21). The `downloading` claim stands: only a start makes a job download again, and a start takes a new
   epoch (`Job.epoch`, whose doc said a supersede and an abandon bump it too, which they do not). The arm is Reached in
   cycle 21 (Shape A, under "Step 7").

### Step 2, continued: candidates 1 and 2, and a sibling

Each pair is its failing test, run red on the HEAD before its fix (P3), then the fix; every fix passed the Sync bundle
(571, 572 and 573 tests: `.build-s3f/c21/c1-sync.log`, `c2-sync.log`, `mb-sync.log`, 1-minute loads 4.81 to 12.96).
The tests are in `EngineFollowBarrierRunClaimTests.swift`; no await is added, so no REENTRANCY row changes.

- **Candidate 1** (`25c1da0` red, `cefbe44` fix): `barrierKeepsARunsClaimAtTheVerdictItWaitsBehind` failed swept first
  on `adfc1ad` as recorded under "Step 1" (`c1-red.log`). Fix: `checkRunSettled` returns while a waiting run
  join (`joinsAfterFollow`) targets a claim the run still holds on that transfer: the join's replay, later in the
  batch, lands the claim, and the drain's end checks the run again. The narrow condition, not a check deferred for
  the whole batch: a run that settles at a verdict mid-batch starts a pending run whose claims join jobs before the
  batch's later verdicts, as a visit-first engine's did. Drop-mutant (`if false, …`): the test fails 2/2 swept first
  (`mut-c1-drop.log`).
- **Candidate 2** (`4337567` red, `0a06be2` fix): `barrierKeepsARunsClaimReroutedBehindAVerdict` failed swept first
  (fetched 0; `c2-red.log`). Fix: `recordRunOutcome` subtracts the delivered ids from the transfer's claims, as
  `releaseRunClaim` and the group arm do, instead of emptying them. The old line put back: the test fails 2/2 swept
  first (`mut-c2-drop.log`). The other ids a transfer can still claim when its outcome arrives are re-routed by their
  callers before or after the run check: `committed`'s deferred ids in `resolveAll`'s `then` (before it); the drain's
  moved-before ids after it, which is the sibling below.
- **The sibling, a run's claim the drain takes off a verdict's job before the verdict: breaks S3-R16 item 1; found
  while fixing candidate 2** (`51ee67a` red, `68666e7` fix). `barrierKeepsARunsClaimTakenOffBeforeAVerdict`: the
  run claims zz-a and zz-b on J; v3 maps zz-a to k while the follow is owed; J's 404 waits with zz-a moved before it
  (`AttemptEnd.movedBefore`); v4 maps zz-a back. `followVisitedFirst`: fetched 1 (zz-a, from a new job of J's
  content), failures [zz-b `.notFound`]. `sweepFollowsFirst`: the drain takes zz-a off J before the verdict and
  re-routes it after (`takeOffMovedBefore`, `rerouteMovedBefore`), and the run check the verdict makes in between,
  the barrier read down, settles the run without the claim: fetched 0, zz-a `.cancelled` (`mb-probe.log`); with the
  old `recordRunOutcome` line it was fetched 0 and zz-a left out of the report (`mut-mb-oldcode.log`), so the break
  predates this cycle. Blocking (P3). Fix: the take-off sets `EngineState.runClaimTakenOff` when it takes a run's
  claim off, `checkRunSettled` waits while it is set, and `rerouteMovedBefore` clears it; the drain's end checks the
  run. Drop-mutants, 2/2 swept first each: the guard (`mut-mb-guard.log`) and the set (`mut-mb-set.log`) fail the
  test's report expectations; without the clear the run never settles, and the test fails at its time limit
  (`mut-mb-clear.log`, 192 s a run).

### Step 3: item A, item 6 and candidate 4

Each pair is its failing test or pin, committed red on its own on the HEAD before its fix (P3), then the fix. The Sync
bundle passed after each fix: 582 tests on `96ca019` (`sync-k4.log`), 583 on `68ce0d7` (`c4-sync.log`, 1-minute load
5.09 at the end). The release build passed on `4783403` (`release-a.log`). Logs are under `.build-s3f/c21/`. Only
`scheduleDrainFollowUp`'s existing await changes, so the REENTRANCY rows are unchanged (RE-S45 stays as it was).

- **Item A** (`cbc9b36` red, `4783403` fix, `02da8e3` T1-space; ruling S3-R26 item 2; `integrate-c21.md` A2–A10, A12,
  K1–K3).
  - *Red on `be0e118`* (`step3-red.log`): `deferBehindVerdictTurns`' longest held turn, best of 3, was 36.81 (404,
    group), 36.50 (timeout, group), 36.54 (404, users) and 36.55 ms (timeout, users), with the heartbeat within 0.01 ms
    of each, against `c2Budget` (10 ms), at 1-minute loads of 11.77 to 9.90. A-T1 failed swept first in all four
    groupings (`EngineFollowBarrierDeferBucketTests.swift:260` on `cbc9b36`: after a held follow turn the queue held O's verdict and
    the joins inserted behind it), and passed visited first (`a-t1-red.log`).
  - *The fix*, as specified: `VerdictKey` and `JoinBehindVerdict` (A2); `EventAfterFollow.verdictKey`, an exhaustive
    switch (A3); `EngineState.joinsBehindVerdicts` (A4); `deferBehindVerdict` registers the join and appends it to its
    verdict's bucket, two O(1) writes (A5); the drain's batch formation places each verdict's bucket right behind it,
    newest first, with the joins it has no room for at the queue's head (A6); `followedLane` walks the buckets (A7);
    the purge walks them at their verdict's position, newest first (A8); the invariants recount them there (K2) and
    report a bucket without exactly one waiting event (K1) or with a stamp past the history (K3) (A9); shutdown clears
    them (A10). A12's expectations count the bucket joins (`SyncBench.joinsBehindVerdicts`).
  - *After* (`bench-defer-a.log`, `4783403`): longest held turn best 4.81, 5.48, 5.48 and 5.52 ms, heartbeat best
    7.54, 7.47, 7.56 and 7.47 ms, 38 turns a run, at 1-minute loads of 5.76 to 5.31: **met**. Re-measured after

    visit-first engine's visit joined the job in its attempt and the verdict answers it. A bucket made for a verdict of
    the batch being drained follows it once it replays, newest first, as its bucket would have followed it into the
    batch; a verdict the batch has not reached when the turn ends goes back to the queue's head with the rest, its
    bucket kept (K1 holds at every turn's end). `AttemptEnd.copy` lives while the verdict waits (`endDeferral` clears
    the record). The 10 cases pass (`c4-green.log`), and the Sync bundle (583 tests).

- **The commit turn's and `followedLane`'s fix** (after `f4f35bd`, the five pins' red commit). `committed` classifies
  each unbound id by its entry in the copy against the job's (`sameTransfer`; a job's entry is its transfer's,
  `addInterest`), no transfer formatted. A commit that re-routes at once is unchanged: it trims, then makes the moved
  re-routes, then answers. One that owes them answers through `resolveAll(_:with:boundOnly:then:)` and does not trim:
  each interest is answered only its bound ids (its unbound ids counted without an allocation; a partly bound one
  copied, a wholly unbound one skipped), and the terminal events read the lane of the interests answered
  (`Job.lane(counting:)`, `publishTerminal(job:outcome:lane:)`), so the answers, the run's claims, the groups' pending
  members, the heals and the events are those of the trimmed job; only the delivery order is the untrimmed table's, an
  accepted order (S3-R16 item 2), as the trimmed table's was. `followedLane`'s `.reroutes` arm checks the content
  before the binding, which it then reads at the job's own transfer, and `rerouteListing` reads a layer's `ends` only
  where the layer has one. **T-ANNOUNCE-OWED** (`EngineFollowBarrierRerouteAnnounceTests.swift`, both orders, the
  kept id wanted by a bulk group and by a prefetch group): the owing commit and the at-once commit announce the same

  maps the ids to Z's content, between X's commit and the replay, the probe **breaks in both orders**: W1…W3 get Z's
  24 bytes and Z is requested, where a visit-first engine's commit of X had re-routed them under K1's copy, onto W
  publishing, whose failure answered them (`owedRerouteWhosePinCommittedFollowsTheCopyAtThatCommit`, seed 2,027,491),
  or, K1 not listing them, with `.notFound` (`owedRerouteWhosePinCommittedEndsUnderTheCopyAtThatCommit`, T21, seed

  no-later-apply test passing). The fix starts from the judge's "layer per commit" (`judge-rr21.md`, open questions)
  in its smallest form: no copy is kept, since the copy in force at a commit is one the batch already holds. A commit
  while a batch waits keeps its attempt (`VerdictKey`) with `copySerial` then (`EngineState.reroutePinCommits`, set
  in `committed`: one insert). `rerouteListing`, at a layer whose pinned job left its end, takes the copy in force at
  that commit, the batch's layer `serial - batch.serial` (a batch holds a layer per copy adopted since it was owed) or
  the engine's copy, and walks on from that layer; without a kept commit (a job requeued or superseded behind its
  verdict) it follows the engine's copy as before, rr21-T8b's class, exact unless the requeued job publishes again
  across a later apply (the judge's approximation; **residual risk**). The records go when the last batch is replayed
  whole (`continueReroutes`) and at shutdown. Clauses (`followBarrierViolations`): no kept commit while no batch waits,
  none for an attempt still at its end, none at a copy not yet adopted. Tests with the fix:
  `owedRerouteWhosePinCommittedFollowsTheAppliesAfterThatCommit` (K2 while W downloads: the walk goes on from the
  commit's copy and K2 moves W1…W3 to Z, 24 bytes each, Z requested once; it passes without the fix too, which follows
  the engine's copy there), `invariantsReportCommitsKeptForOwedReroutes` (each clause broken alone; X's commit kept
  with the copy's serial then, forgotten after the last batch) and `shutdownForgetsTheCommitsKeptForOwedReroutes`.

  R18 (`integrate-rr21.md`) with RR21-HOP's join variant (`2c62e85`): a listed join that waits in `eventsAfterFollow`
  carries a chain (`JoinChain`: `copySerial` when it deferred and a layer per copy adopted since; `addInterest`), which
  `layerOwedReroutes` extends at each apply by the batches' rule (the jobs publishing at the apply, and the exit
  verdicts waiting behind the join, from its second layer on only those deferred after its last layer's apply), one
  layer shared by the joins of a stretch of the queue with no verdict between them. `replayJoin` and `followedLane`
  read the join's copy through it (`joinListing`, the batches' walk, now `followLayers`): a job still at the attempt's
  end a layer pinned holds the join, whose end answers or re-routes it as the job's own interests; one that committed
  hands it the copy in force at that commit. A join behind a waiting verdict (`joinsBehindVerdicts`) and an unlisted
  one carry no chain and follow the engine's copy, as before. The kept commits (`reroutePinCommits`) are now recorded
  while any event waits for the follow, since a join's pin needs them with no batch waiting (`joinGapDropped`), and
  kept until the barrier is down (`endWorldHistory`) or shutdown, no longer until the last batch's replay: PIN-END's
  clause "none while no batch waits" becomes "none once the barrier is down", and
  `invariantsReportCommitsKeptForOwedReroutes` checks the new message and the forgetting at the barrier's end (a test
  of this cycle, changed with the clause it checks). A new clause checks each chain's length against the copies adopted
  since its join deferred (`invariantsReportAWaitingJoinsChainWithoutItsCopies`, seed 2,027,441: an injected layer is
  reported exactly, and the drain then joins J). Residual: a join requeued or superseded behind its pin follows the
  engine's copy, as a batch's re-route does (the judge's approximation; **residual risk**).

  joins wait for an owed follow over 10,000 changed members, `followedLane` over them, and the drain through two

  consumes the event and makes it again, so no layer array is shared while it grows, and the pass reads the engine's

  and the engine's copy maps the join's id elsewhere (the walk can only turn a reach away then: a pin of another job
  still at its end, or a copy that dropped the id). The only caller decides a downloading job's 429, so the job is never
  at an attempt's end there: the `atEnd` term keeps the shortcut exact for any job, and a mutant that drops it is

- **rr21-C6: site 2** (R6 and R7; the commit after `c99d82a`). `takeOffMovedBefore(_:)` takes the transfer, not a copy
  of the job, and changes the job in place: the held ids are the job's ids that `AttemptEnd.movedBefore` lists; their
  holders come from the index (`Job.moveItems(of:)`, O(held + holders)), each token's lane and kind read once; a partial
  interest loses its held ids (`subtractAssets`), and the wholly held interests are removed in ascending token order
  (`removeInterest`), so that a job a claim keeps holds the last one's lane (`Job.heldLane`), as the sorted walk over
  every interest left it (only the wholly held tokens are sorted now). It returns the re-route items, unsorted, and the
  held ids some interest holds. The replays (`replayVerdict`, the `.spaceFailure` arm) bind no copy of the job: each
  reads `movesAfterVerdict` first, takes off, ends the deferral (`attemptEnd = nil`; `endDeferral` is removed), and
  decides once, before the verdict (`chargeTakeOff`): ids that fit the turn's `drainIDsLeft` are charged to it and made
  after the verdict and its visit, in today's order, by token and then id (`rerouteMovedBefore`); ids that do not fit
  spend the turn (`drainIDsLeft = 0`), so the visit after the verdict moves nothing in it and leaves its whole move as
  the follow's rest (`startMove` with no budget), and the replay returns the batch (`oweReroutes`), which the drain's
  break puts back at the queue's head (`landTakeOff`; R8's order: the verdict, the visit's rest, the batch, the
  verdict's bucket newest first, its overflow, later events). `runClaimTakenOff` is cleared once the batch is owed, whose
  counter then holds the run check (`reroutesWaiting`). `replay` returns `EventAfterFollow?` from both arms. Since
  `drainIDsLeft` never goes below 0 (`continueReroutes` and the visits spend at most what is left), an owing take-off has
  at least one id, so no empty batch is owed. A test of this cycle changed with the fix (G3): rr21-T3's `:43` searched
  every turn for m05's re-joined interest, which O0 holds until the take-off, so it found the setup's reading; it now
  searches the turns after the verdict's, and also requires the verdict's turn to have taken the interest off
  (stricter; on `42a3689` it fails, the take-off re-joining it in the verdict's turn). Results: the five site-2 tests
  pass in both orders (12 cases, `each/c6-fix-2.log`), and the whole Sync suite passes (661 tests in 56 suites,
  `each/c6-fix-sync1.log`, 307.6 s, 1-minute loads 10.51 to 6.37).
- **rr21-C6: the take-off in one access** (the commit after `e437c28`). The site-2 pins on `e437c28`
  (`each/c6-pins-fix.out`, `each/c6-pins-fix-1.log`, release, under `sim.lock`, 1-minute loads 6.49 before and 8.64
  after) pass their setups and miss C2 (`BenchSyncRerouteTakeOff.swift:57:9` and `:58:9`, twice each): the verdict's
  turn takes 27.66 ms (29.11, 28.56, 27.66; heartbeat 27.66) for 10,000 user waiters all held and 17.48 ms (17.48,
  19.93, 17.87; heartbeat 17.52) half held; 5,000 moved before and 5,000 after take 5.54 ms (5.95, 5.54, 11.39), and
  rr21-C3's pin (`movedBeforeDrainTurns`, its longest actor wait) 6.04 ms (6.04, 6.09, 10.78), within. The per-token work was each wholly held
  interest's removal through the engine (`removeInterest`, `dropInterest`): several lookups and copies of the job (its
  lane, the claim key, `relane`'s read) and an observer pass (`notifyObservers`), once per token. `Job.takeOff(_:)` now
  takes the held ids off in one access to the job: the index's holders, the count per token, whole or partial decided
  before any change, the items read from each interest, the partial interests' subtraction, then the removals in
  ascending token order with the job's lane read before each (`JobTakeOff.laneBeforeFirst`, `laneBeforeLast`).
  `dropInterest`'s tail is `settleRemoval(_:before:last:)`, which the take-off calls once after its last removal and
  `dropInterest` after its one: a job left with no interest holds `last`, its lane before the last removal
  (`Job.heldLane`), kept for a claim or retired; one left with interests is re-laned from `before`. The equivalence
  with a removal at a time: only the last removal can leave the job empty; a re-lane does nothing to a job `failed`
  with its verdict deferred (`relane`), which every `.attemptFailed` replay's job is (`replayVerdict`'s guard); an
  ENOSPC's job that a user's request re-queued during its free-space read (T20, `spaceFailed`) is re-queued, with a
  fresh ticket, by each re-lane that changes its lane or finds it user-initiated, and by the one re-lane if by any
  (removals never raise a lane), at the last lane: the same place among the other jobs (`enqueue`); the run's `held`
  loses the transfer when its token is among the removed, as the removal of that token did; observers are notified
  once, where each removal notified: no other caller sees the states between two removals of one turn (a `package`
  `waitUntil` predicate that held only between two of them would no longer be resumed; no wait in the suite is one).
  Results (release, `each/c6-pins-one.out`, `each/c6-pins-one-1.log`, under `sim.lock`, 1-minute loads 5.38 before
  and 5.09 after, within S3-R23's 10): all held, the verdict's turn 7.26 ms (7.26, 7.47, 7.30; heartbeat 7.43); half
  held 6.17 ms (6.18, 6.17, 6.23; heartbeat 7.40); 5,000 and 5,000, 5.52 ms (5.58, 5.55, 5.52; heartbeat 5.52); and
  `movedBeforeDrainTurns` 5.12 ms (5.15, 5.21, 5.12; J's 500 deferring 3.00): every site-2 case within C2, with its
  setup. The take-off's 11 tests pass in both orders (`each/c6-one-1.log`), and the whole Sync suite passes (661 tests
  in 56 suites, `each/c6-one-sync1.log`, 298.3 s, 1-minute loads 3.76 to 4.41).
- **rr21-C6: T-shared, RR21-PRESENT-PRUNE at site 2 and PROBE-RR21-RESERVE-REJOIN** (the commit after `8647760`;
  `EngineFollowBarrierRerouteTakeOffShareTests.swift`, with the setup's additions in
  `EngineFollowBarrierRerouteTakeOffFixture.swift`: Y and W for a site-1 batch behind the verdict (`commit`,
  `takeOffHoldY`, `takeOffCommitY`), the present content D and zz-e for the gates (`present`, `TakeOff.v5`,
  `takeOffOpenBreaker`), a capped retry (`capped`), and the readings `yOnW`, `boundOnD`, `dJob` and `jobs`).
  - T-shared (`verdictsVisitAndTheOwedBatchBehindItShareTheDrainTurnsIDs`): O0 times out with three ids zz-c0p00…p02
    that v4 maps to P, and Y (zz-yk, zz-y00…y02) publishes, held, while v4 maps zz-y00…y02 to W, so Y's commit owes
    their three re-routes as one batch behind O0's verdict (site 1; the queue `[verdict, reroutes]`, required).
    Swept first the verdict's turn moves the visit's three p-ids and makes one of the batch's re-routes, its four ids;
    the next turn makes the other two (re-routes `[1, 2]`), and no turn moves and re-routes more than four. A turn's
    re-routes are read from the batch's `owedIDs`, not from W's job, whose publication can land between two readings.
    Both orders: P serves the p-ids, Y zz-yk and W the moved zz-y…, O0's retry zz-c0k, and no job is left.
  - RR21-PRESENT-PRUNE at site 2 (`owedTakeOffOntoAPresentContentIsServedFromTheStore`, rr21-B24; three gates):
    D (zz-d, 4,000 bytes) is made present after v2; O0 holds zz-c0k, six moved-before ids and zz-c0p00, and ends in
    a 404 whose second attempt is held; v4 maps the six back to O0's content and zz-c0p00 to P, v5 maps the six to D,
    so its apply binds them to D's blob. Swept first the drain's 404 ends O0 and its take-off re-routes the six under
    v5 and owes them (six past four a turn): no job holds them, so the idle pass after the verdict's turn would drop
    their bindings were the batch not waiting (`pruneBoundContent`'s `eventsAfterFollow.isEmpty` guard), and the
    replay answers them from the store. Visited first v3's visit moved them onto N, the 404 was given at its arrival,
    v4's visit moved them to a fresh job of O0's content, held, and v5's to D, where the store served them. The
    design's three lessons: (1) v4 cannot map them to D itself: the owed visit that meets O0 while its set serves the
    follow re-routes the moved-before ids at once (`rerouteOnVisit`, `Job.rerouteFor`), so no take-off was left; v5
    lands once that visit spent the set (`takeOffFollowUntilVisited`), and its own visit passes O0 and leaves the six to
    the verdict. (2) A pass finds O0 only by an id whose content differs between its copy and the engine's
    (`continueFollowScans`): the six are on O0's content in v2's and v4's copies and on N's, which has no job swept
    first, in v3's, so without zz-c0p00 no pass of v4's follow visited O0, its set was never spent and its verdict was
    given in the follow's last turn (`each/c6-present-diag.log`: four follow turns, O0 never in the follow's order, its
    set of six unspent); zz-c0p00 makes v2's pass find O0 at v4's apply, whose visit passes it to the verdict, which
    answers it with the 404 in both orders. (3) The gates close after v5 in both orders: closed before v3 the breaker
    failed visit-first's N job fast, and with the timeout ending T20 re-queued O0 at v4 and its retry served 16 bytes
    before v5, hence the 404 with a held second attempt. zz-e's held 403 opens the breaker at its arrival
    (`recordBreaker`, `authDistinctAssets` 1; zz-e's waiter gets it); offline is awaited swept first only, since
    visited first the engine is idle after v5 and its watcher gone (`reconcileIdle`); `insufficientSpace` leaves
    1,000 bytes. Swept first the test requires that the verdict's turn ends O0 and owes the six as one batch with all
    six bound to D after it, the batch answers four ids a turn then two, no job is made after v5 (`jobsCreated`) and
    none of D's content, and the invariants hold; both orders expect D's bytes for the six, the 404 for zz-c0k and

  - PROBE-RR21-RESERVE-REJOIN (`takeOffAtTheReservationsEdgeRejoinsItsJobWithItsRetryState`; the order class of

### rr21-C7: the mutation table, the survivors and R19's records

**The runs.** Every mutant was applied to a copy of the sources named in its file's heading (the copy-based runners
`tools/mut21.py`, `mut21s.py`, `mut21u.py`, with the item lists in `tools/mut-*.py`; item 5's and T20's were applied to
the worktree one at a time and reverted), built in debug, and run twice on its item's tests; a mutant both runs left
alive ran once more on the whole Sync bundle. A hang past the run's time limit counts as a kill, as a test's time limit
does; a run that crashed counts too (each crash in the table is the runtime's trap on a continuation resumed twice).
"Item runs" marks each run by the orders of its failing test cases (integrate-rr21.md C7's per-order counts): **S** a
case run `sweepFollowsFirst`, **V** one run `followVisitedFirst`, **U** a test with no order argument, **H** a hang,
**C** a crash, `pass` none. `FB` stands for `EngineFollowBarrier` and a file's `Tests.swift` is left out. The marks are
read from the runs' logs (`tools/muttable.py`, `tools/perorder.py`); a mutant run again in a later file keeps its later
logs. A kill in `S` only is a branch whose state arises swept first. S3-R26 item 12's answer 1 counts it reached in
both orders when its test asserts the visit-first answers in both and the draft cites why `followVisitedFirst` cannot
reach it, or the test requires the state per order (as Shape A does, under "Step 7"); that is recorded with each test
where Steps 1 to 7 describe it, and this table does not re-check it.

claimed). Each names the state where it would change an answer; no test this cycle builds it.

- `vy-owed-moves-too` (`EngineMoves.swift:308`, `listing == nil ?` to `true ?`): the passing rule also on an owed
  move (`continueInbound`, whose `listing` is the move's copy). It decides when the move's holder is publishing with a
  moved id among the ids its publication began with that the copy mapped elsewhere (`rerouteOnVisit`): the mutant leaves
  the id's interests to the holder's visit, which re-routes them later, behind the target's waiting verdict, where the
  move put them on the target before it. The state: a holder publishing (held) after an apply behind the barrier, then
  the target's attempt ending with its verdict deferred while the move off the holder is owed.
- `b22-no-waiter-owner`, `b22-no-run-owner` (`EngineFailures.swift:860`, `:868`): `followedLane` counts an owed item
  only while its waiter still waits for it at the batch's job, or its run is the engine's. A cancel's removal waits
  behind the batch and marks the token withdrawn (rr21-T12's `cancelled` shape passes under both mutants), so the guards
  decide only for an owner that left by a path that leaves no waiting removal (a waiter answered from the store, a run
  replaced) before a verdict whose lane the item would raise. Not shown unreachable.
- `b23-no-lane`, `b23-no-kind` (`EngineCommands.swift:1066`): the purge arm withdraws the owed non-user, non-waiter
  items of purged ids. The mutants would also withdraw a user-lane group member's item, or a prefetch-lane waiter's;
  rr21-T13's batch holds user waiters and a prefetch group only. Extending it with both kinds would decide them.
- `f7-delisted-stays` (`EngineDispatch.swift:1152`, `?? false` to `?? true`): a commit's unbound id the copy no longer
  lists is classified as staying; captured, it sets `refused` and the commit holds the content for a manifest catch-up
  (`holdForManifest`), which the correct classification never does for a delisted id. Its answer, `.notFound`, is the
  same; the hold is the difference no test reads.
- `p7-forget-at-last-batch` (`EngineFollow.swift:760`): forgetting `reroutePinCommits` when the last batch is made.
  Waiting joins' chains also read them (`followLayers`), so a chained join behind the last batch, pinned to a job that
  committed, would follow another copy. No test has such a join behind the last batch.
- `r2b-made-ignores-previous`, `r2c-made-ignores-verdicts` (`EngineFollow.swift:702`): `layerOwedReroutes`' cache of
  the last layer made. Without either key a layer is reused for an event whose last layer's apply, or whose verdicts
  behind it, differ, so its `ends` can miss a verdict that a visit-first engine's visit met at its end. The state: two
  owing events deferred across an apply, with a verdict behind both deferred between their applies.
- `r5-lane-engine-copy` (`EngineFailures.swift:843`): a waiting join's reach read under the engine's copy instead of
  its chain's (R18's `joinListing`). It decides for a chained join whose chain pins its id to a copy that maps it
  differently from the engine's, met by a verdict whose lane it would raise.
- `r7-fast-ignores-end`, `r8-fast-any-join` (`EngineFailures.swift:840`): the fast path that passes a chained join the
  copy maps elsewhere. r7 passes it also while the job is at an attempt's end (where a pin of this job can hold it); r8
  passes an unchained join too, which an unlisted join's own entry (`join.entry`) can still bring to this job. Each
  needs a lane-deciding verdict with such a join waiting.

**R19's arguments** (`integrate-rr21.md`).

- *Site 1, call for call.* A commit whose answers and re-routes fit `inboundIDsNow` together makes the calls a
  commit made before RR-21, in the same order (`committed`, `EngineDispatch.swift:1163-1190`): the trims, then the
  moved items' `reroute`s sorted by token and id, then `resolveAll`, whose closure, after the job's removal, holds for
  the manifest when an id was refused and makes the deferred items' `reroute`s in the same sort. Only a commit that does
  not fit owes, and it then makes none of its re-routes at once (`boundOnly`, `deferReroutes`).
- *Site 2's charge and its two orders* (recorded under "Step 5", rr21-C6): a take-off is charged to the drain turn's
  `drainIDsLeft` before the verdict, so a fitting one is made after the verdict and its visit, in today's order, and
  one that does not fit spends the turn and is owed as one batch right behind the verdict and the visit's rest (R8's
  order); `PROBE-RR21-RESERVE-REJOIN` holds at the edge and past it.
- *The release* (`releaseRerouteHolds`, `EngineFollow.swift:827`): it resumes every publication's wait once the last
  batch is made. Only the drain makes owed re-routes (`continueReroutes`, from `replay`), the drain runs only while no
  follow is owed (`drainEventsAfterFollow`'s guard; `followOwed` covers `inboundOwed` and `followMoving`), it stops at
  the first event after which a visit's rest is owed (`followMoving`), and no replay owes a move then (`bringInbound`
  returns unless a follow is owed). So when the counter reaches 0, `inboundBlocks` is false for every job and each
  resumed publication binds: a filter `!inboundBlocks` on the waits it resumes would keep every one (the design's
  filter, which `integrate-rr21.md`'s amendments removed under S3-R16 item 3, was never written). Shutdown resumes
  every wait (`releaseInboundWaits`) and zeroes the counter (`EngineShutdown.swift:129`).
- *Removed and Equivalent branches*: the two removals above; `integrate-rr21.md`'s own removals from its design, never
  written (`withdrawPurgedJoins`' early return, the layer append's guard, the sites' `!followOwed &&
  !drainingAfterFollow`, the release's `!inboundBlocks` filter, the drain's `left != nil` disjunct; its
  amendments_decided); and the Equivalent survivors above.

### Step 6: item C, Phase 2

- **The trigger** (S3-R26 item 4). On `e5b4df9` with `06d5e40`'s pin (`each/c12-red.out`, release, under `sim.lock`,
  1-minute loads 9.69 before and 7.45 after), best of 3: `commitTurns(.waiters)`'s own turn 11.27 ms (heartbeat
  11.51), above the 7.0 ms trigger; `waitersStalledSubscriber` 14.44 ms; `groupStalledSubscriber` 8.75; `manyGroups`
  10.01; two stalled subscribers 18.04 (recorded, not gated); and `commitWaitersBoundTurns` (`06d5e40`: 10,000 user
  waiters all bound, owing nothing) 11.56. Phase 2 applies.
- **C12** (`28d533e`). A resolution of more than `answersPerTurn` (512) interests computes every waiter's answer and
  takes every waiter and every settled ensure out of the state in its own turn, and leaves only the resumes to the
  answer follow-ups, oldest first, `answersPerTurn` a turn (`owedAnswers`, `answerFollowUp`); shutdown resumes the rest
  with their stored values (`drainEverything`). Each caller gets the value it got when every resume was made in the
  commit's turn; only the moment it returns moves (the table's order of resumes, an accepted order, S3-R26 item 10). The
  owed answers have an invariant clause, and the commit pins' windows end at the last resume. T-A1 to T-A5 and the
  ensure arm (`EngineOwedAnswersTests.swift`) run in both orders at four a turn; 18 of the 19 Phase 2 mutants are killed
  2/2 (`mut21-c12.txt`, `mut21-c12b.txt`), and `c12-no-running-guard` is Equivalent (under "rr21-C7").
- **Figures after C12** (on `28d533e`, `each/c12-green.out`, 1-minute loads 8.65 before and 8.11 after), best of 3:
  `.waiters` 7.89 ms (its own turn 7.89), `waitersStalledSubscriber` 10.77 (**miss**), `groupStalledSubscriber` 9.09,
  `manyGroups` 10.57 (**miss**), two subscribers 14.35 (recorded), `waitersBound` 7.64, and 10,000 user waiters moved
  onto one content with 511 joins behind the batch 7.68 ms.
- **`manyGroups`** (`57d5d8c`). Every pump runs `materializeEnsures`, which sorted every group's token to visit the
  ensure groups with fetches left: 10,000 one-member prefetch groups' tokens at a commit's pump. It now sorts only those
  candidates, in the order it visited them: a group's kind never changes, its fetches are only consumed, and nothing in
  the loop registers a group. The whole Sync suite passes (678 tests in 56 suites, `each/ensure-sort-sync.log`).
- **Figures on `2c351e8`** (`each/c12-sort.out`, release, under `sim.lock`, 1-minute loads 4.18 before and 4.33 after),
  best of 3: `.waiters` 7.27 ms (7.62, 7.35, 7.27; its own turn 7.27); `waitersStalledSubscriber` **10.31** (10.68,
  10.31, 19.50); `groupStalledSubscriber` 8.71 (8.74, 9.40, 8.71), at the edge; `manyGroups` 9.34 (9.38, 9.34, 10.93),
  at the edge; two stalled subscribers 13.74 (13.74, 13.97, 13.90), recorded, not gated; `waitersBound` 7.41; and the
  511 joins behind the batch 7.45 (its longest held turn 3.11).
- **The miss, blocking and reported** (S3-R26 item 4: "A miss Phase 2 cannot cut is blocking and reported").
  `waitersStalledSubscriber` misses `c2Budget` by 0.31 ms at a quiet load. The stalled subscriber holds an event per id
  of the commit (the pin's setup requires `run.buffered` of 10,000 or more), and each costs about 0.3 µs a subscriber in
  the commit's turn: 10.31 − 7.27 = 3.04 ms for one subscriber, 6.47 ms for two. Phase 2 owes only the waiters' and the
  ensures' resumes (S3-R26 item 4), and terminal events stay ascending in the commit's turn (S3-R26 answer 2), so no
  change within the rulings cuts it. The routes, which are the owner's to rule on: owe the events past the commit's
  turn in their order, as the answers are owed, or carry many ids in one event (an event-shape change). The
  two-subscriber figure is "open, for the owner" (answer 4).

### Step 7: item 5 (`waitingTarget`'s queued arm) and its two probes

- **Shape A** (`4aeb321`, `EngineFollowBarrierWaitingTargetTests.swift`'s
  `barrierMakesAMoveOntoAJobItsDrainedPublicationReQueued`): T's drained publication fails ENOENT while v3b's walk owes
  the move H → T [zz-x]; swept first, the follow turn that makes the owed moves finds T queued at the move's epoch, the
  arm. It is Reached under S3-R26 item 12's answer 1: the test runs in both orders, asserts the visit-first answers in
  both, and requires per order the state (swept first the owed move, visited first none, since v3's visit moved zz-x
  onto T while it published); the fold mutant (`i5-pin-fold`) fails the one-turn state assertion 2/2, and rr21-T8b
  (`RerouteRequeue:124`, `:130`) kills it in both orders.
- **Probe (ii)**, the later apply (`3412ec3`, then `d85eb02` with the re-queued job in the turn's follow order; both red
  swept first): v4 maps zz-x to a third content U while T's drained publication runs; the ENOENT re-queues T and its
  fresh attempt gets a 404. Visited first, v4's visit passed T with zz-x on it and the 404 answered X; swept first the
  owed move onto T was dropped and H's visit sent zz-x to U, so X got U's bytes and U started once: an answer
  difference, blocking (S3-R16 1(a)). **Fixed** (`58b278e`): the move is made onto the queued job at its epoch, its end
  still recorded (`waitingTarget(_:)`), and an owed visit passes such a job as still publishing while no apply was
  followed since its end, else moves its ids as met queued (`rerouteOnVisit`'s queued arm). A fourth test covers an
  apply after the end (`barrierMovesAReQueuedJobsIdForAnApplyAfterItsEnd`). Shape A's assertion changed with the fix,
  one to one (G3): `afterTurn.h == [t.x.identifier] && afterTurn.t == [t.a.identifier]` (the move dropped) became
  `afterTurn.h == nil && afterTurn.t == [t.a.identifier, t.x.identifier]` (the move made, H gone), and its setup's
  `#require` gained `&& requeued.end` (the end still recorded). The whole Sync suite passed (674 tests in 56 suites,
  `each/i5-fix-sync.log`).
- **Probe (i)**, the T20 window (`2130e61`, `EngineFollowBarrierSpaceReadTests.swift`; `analyse-g4-reach.md`'s Shape
  B): an ENOSPC's free-space read runs a follow turn behind the barrier whose join re-lanes the failed job before its
  verdict defers, and a user interest's T20 re-queues it, so the verdict is skipped (`decideSpaceFailure` returns for a
  queued job). Swept first, at an interactive cap of one attempt, A and X got T's bytes from a second request, where a
  visit-first engine's verdict answered both with the space figures and requested T once: red in `sweepFollowsFirst` at
  `:93`, `:102`, `:103` and `:104`, walked or not (`each/i5-probe1-red.log`, 8 issues), passing visited first.
  **Fixed** (`dff8946`): the follow's own visit or move made with no apply since the publication's end leaves the job
  failed (`relane`'s failed arm), as a visit-first engine's visit met it publishing. Two controls hold the clause's
  sides: a user request after a publication's failure with no follow skips the backoff (`EngineRunPathTests`), and a
  visit for an apply made after the end skips it too, in both orders (`each/i5-probe1-green.log`,
  `each/i5-t20-controls.log`). The first control failed once in a whole-suite run (`each/t20-sync.log`, `:288`: its job
  was read after its re-queued attempt had begun); it now accepts a job no longer failed or gone (`!= false`), its
  other expectations (the second attempt's bytes, two requests) unchanged, and the suite then passed twice (677 and 678
  tests, `each/t20-sync2.log`, `each/t20-sync3.log`).
- **The transfer's sibling** (`analyse-g4-reach.md` (c)): a transfer's ENOSPC sets its job failed before its resume
  point's and free-space reads, and the read's follow turn joined zz-x to it behind the barrier, re-queueing it (T20):

  `each/t20-transfer-red.log`, `-red2.log`). **Fixed** (`b171e8b`): the transfer's end is recorded
  (`Job.transferSpaceEnd`), `relane`'s failed arm reads it as it reads a publication's end, and a start clears it
  (`each/t20-transfer-green.log`, 4 tests).
- **The docs** (`46e3669`): `enqueue`'s list of the paths that give a place behind the barrier, `Job.epoch`'s (only
  creation and a start take one), and the cycle-20 draft's one-path claim, corrected under it.
- **Mutants**: `i5-move-drop`, `i5-visit-drop` and `i5-visit-no-applies` killed 2/2 (S), `i5-pin-fold` 2/2 (S and

### Step 8: the close

- **The first gate run** (`.build-s3f/c21/gates21.sh` on `2c351e8`, the code of `28c2700`, from 14:45:40; logs under
  `.build-s3f/c21/gates/`). The benchmarks failed only on their two known issues, P-13 (WP-B's) and
  `waitersStalledSubscriber`'s miss (reported, "Step 6"); `verify.sh --quick`, the release build, the two gates, the
  first two Sync runs and TSan passed. The third Sync run failed (`15:23:50 sync3 exit 1`), with one issue, the flake
  below. The run was stopped once TSan ended (`tools/stop-after-tsan.sh`): its next stages would have built the fix.
  Every stage ran again on the fixed HEAD (`gates21b.sh`, under "Gate evidence (cycle 21)").
- **The reservation-edge flake** (`PROBE-RR21-RESERVE-REJOIN`, `(.sweepFollowsFirst, .atTheEdgeCapped)`; `sync3.log`):
  `EngineFollowBarrierRerouteTakeOffShareTests.swift:167:17: Expectation failed: made[given - 1] == moved &&
  turns[given].batches == 0`, with `made` [0, 0, 0, 0]. The verdict's turn was read as `follow owed=false … verdicts=0
  settled=0 batches=0/0 queue=[](0) … o0=0 … jobs=0`: O0 was already gone. Its other expectations, the visit-first
  answers among them, held. The quick run, the first two Sync runs and both of reqs #7's whole-suite mutant runs passed
  it. The third Sync run ran at a 1-minute load of mean 20.88 (5.12 to 32.51; `suite-load.txt`), beside those mutant
  runs.
  - **The mechanism, a test race.** At the edge, the verdict's turn is the drain's last: it leaves the barrier down,
    and its pump starts O0's retry at once (the pump admits nothing behind the barrier, `pump`). The take-off's user
    re-routes joined O0 while it was backed off, and a user-initiated join skips the backoff (T20, `relane`'s failed
    arm), as v4's visit's join did visited first. The fake runs the capped retry's `.fail` inside `transfer(_:)`, and
    its verdict at the cap answers all five ids and ends O0. `takeOffTurns` reads the turn in its next actor call. When
    the retry's driver reaches the engine first, the reading shows O0 gone. The engine's answers are the same in both
    orders.
  - **Red first** (S3-R26 item 11: the shape exists before the fix). `a380c78` adds `takeOffTurns`' `settle` step.
    After a turn that leaves the barrier down, the test waits until O0's retry has its terminal, held or applied, and
    then reads the turn: the worst order the scheduler may give (PROBE-C21-RESERVE-SETTLE). It fails 2/2 at `:179`, the
    same expectation, with the same readings (`.build-s3f/c21/flake/red-run.log`, `red-run2.log`).
  - **The fix** (`e599ae1`). While `takeOffTurns` reads the held turns, it holds the attempts' terminals
    (`holdAttemptTerminals()`), and it releases them with the follow-ups. With the settle step it passes 2/2
    (`green-run1.log`, `green-run2.log`), and the ten `takeOffTurns` tests pass 2/2 (`family1.log`, `family2.log`).
  - **The test changes** (G3, one to one; the test and the fixture are this cycle's, so not in `MIGRATION.md`).
    `takeOffTurns(t)` became `takeOffTurns(t) { … }`, with the settle wait. No expectation changed. The doc comment's
    "rejoin O0, backed off with its retry state" became "rejoin O0 with its retry state (its attempts) … and their user
    waiters' join skips its backoff (T20)".

  asset the store holds (R-NET-6, L4-R5). Splitting them over turns would leave interests in present ids on the job
  between turns, where an outcome of the job could reach them; that state needs its own invariants. Put to the
  orchestrator.
- **PROBE-C21-HOLDERS** (item B's residual 5, under "Step 4": "blocking if a case with h near 10,000 misses `c2Budget`
  at a quiet load"; `ProbeC21Holders.swift` in the same scratch copy). One id, m, of H's content is held by 10,000
  interests: a user waiter each, or a one-member prefetch group each. O, a user request's 16 bytes, downloads, held.
  v3 maps m to O's content, so H's visit moves m with every holder. H holds only m (`ids: 1` before), so the move is
  `move`'s supersede branch: `supersede` without a bound re-routes the 10,000 interests in the visit's turn, as a
  visit's supersede of any job does. `move`'s other branch (a holder keeping other ids) re-routes the same 10,000
  pairs in one turn after sorting them; it was not measured. The heartbeat times the apply's sync and its whole
  follow, as `partialMoveTurns` does, best of 3 after a warm-up at 1,000, in the same apm stage:
  - user waiters: [39.01, 39.16, 39.08] ms, best 39.01;
  - one-member groups: [41.09, 41.56, 40.98], best 40.98.

  Every run ended with O holding both ids and all 10,001 interests, and H with none. Both miss C2 by about four times at
  a quiet load: **blocking**, reported. Alone, in the same re-run as PROBE-C21-APM's: 37.80 ms best with user waiters
  ([38.12, 37.80, 37.93]) and 40.12 with groups ([40.48, 40.93, 40.12]). No route was found within the design: a move
  takes an id whole, all its interests in one turn (`continueMove`), and an owed batch replays each id with all its
  tokens in one drain turn (RR-21's R8). Splitting one id's holders over turns needs a state in which the id has left
  the job while holders still hold it, with that state's own invariants (I2's class). Put to the orchestrator.

  - `EngineCommands.swift:1068`: the purge's `guard !removed.isEmpty else { continue }`. With nothing removed,
    `MinHeap.removeAll(where:)` leaves the heap as it was (no heapify), the loop runs zero times, and the write-back
    stores the same batch. The guard saves that write.

    as `dropInterest` does (`EngineJobs.swift:385`). Only two readers use `run.held`. `finishRun` skips a job without
    the run's interest (`EngineRuns.swift:825`). An invariant clause checks the other direction
    (`EngineCommands.swift:1839`). `removeJob` removes the entry when the job ends. A stale entry costs `finishRun` one
    skipped lookup.

    resolution owes an answer while the engine shuts down. Without the guard, the follow-up resumes nothing, empties an

    One test would reach it and kill the slice's drop-mutant: hold the follow-ups over more than 512 owed answers, shut

  - `EngineFollow.swift:883`: `replayVerdict`'s second guard, for a waiting verdict whose job is no longer failed at

    failed job whose verdict waits (`EngineJobs.swift:307`), and only the verdict schedules its retry. The `.failed`
    half is an `invariantViolations()` clause ("jobs whose failure verdict waits for a follow are not failed"), which
    no test breaks on purpose; the epoch half has no clause. S3-R19 item 3 asks for the guard's removal, or for a
    clause that a test exercises.

### Residual risks and accepted orders (cycle 21)

- **Accepted orders** (S3-R26 item 10; S3-R16 item 2): newest-first joins behind a verdict (item A); the table's order
  of resumes (Phase 2); item 5's order, place and ticket; RR-21's replay order, by id then token, and the places of the
  jobs its replays create; site 2's two orders (at-once re-routes before the visit's rest, owed ones after the whole
  visit), with `PROBE-RR21-RESERVE-REJOIN` holding; and the bulk release of run claims, with rr21-T18. The take-off's
  land sort (`c6-land-desc`, `c6-land-unsorted`) is of the same class.
- **RR-21's residuals** (`integrate-rr21.md`'s residual_risks, each a timing class only while the event lands between
  the two engines' answers, S3-R24 item 5): a cancel or a release between the owing instant and a T21 or present pair's
  replay gives `.cancelled` (ruling 1); the global hold delays unrelated publications, and an apply during it can drop
  a held job's ids (ruling 2); a pin whose job committed, was superseded or was re-queued by ENOENT between the apply
  and the replay follows the copy at the replay, exact unless another apply landed between (ruling 3, rr21-T8b's
  class); a purge's dropped bindings, an eviction or a quarantine between the owing instant and the replay turn a
  present answer into a join (ruling 5); a heal of a T21 system item's asset in that window is forgotten at the replay
  (ruling 1's class; `PROBE-RR21-HEAL-T21` breaks nothing, under "Step 5"); the broad idle guards keep every binding
  and the watcher while any event waits; admissions and run settlement wait for every owed batch (about 20 drain turns
  at 10,000 ids); each owed batch keeps its copy and its layers' outgoing copies alive (memory only).
- **Items 2 to 4**: item A's bucket order is an accepted order (above; under "Step 3"); item B's residual risks are
  listed with their class, condition and test under "Step 4"; item C's are the table's order of resumes (above),
  `waitersStalledSubscriber`'s miss (blocking, under "Step 6") and the two-subscriber figure (for the owner).
- **The open survivors** under "rr21-C7".

**A sequencing deviation, recorded.** Item 10's step 0 asks for the 'before' figure of every case items 1 to 4 add.
Item 1's and item 12.3's cases (items 1 and 2) are measured here. Item 3's PIN-APM and PIN-APM-SPARE need d2's
behaviour-free factoring as their seam, and item 4's cases are built only if item 4's deciding figures trigger them; their
'before' figures are taken at the start of steps 5 and 6, on a scratch copy of `d5b2ab9` with the same seams, so that
the figures are the same `d5b2ab9` figures the ruling asks for. This keeps step 0 short before a likely cut-off by the
weekly limit (item 10, "Expect the weekly limit").

### Step 1: item 12.2 (correct #1), e1-R1 and the probes

**e1-R1** (`5ad245d`, on `b603475`'s red T-E1, T-E3 and T-E4). `EngineState.reroutePinCommits` maps a `VerdictKey` to a
`PinEnd`: the copy's serial at the end and whether the job kept the pinned ids. The ENOENT arm of `publicationFailed`
writes a kept end (`keepsEntry: true`) while events wait, inside `if self.transition(transfer, to: .queued)` (12.5.5);
a commit's write is `keepsEntry: false`. `followLayers` reads a kept end: with no layer adopted since the re-queue the
pin layer's outgoing copy is returned (the ids ride the fresh attempt); otherwise the walk goes on from the first layer
after the re-queue (`index = after + 1`). The ruling's kill table calls that index `next` ("`next < layers.count`",
"`index = next + 1`"); the code calls it `after`, the number of copies adopted from the batch's serial to the end, and
the table's rows apply to it as written. The code docs of `rerouteListing`, `followLayers`, `waitingTarget(_:)`,
`endWorldHistory`, the ENOENT arm, `EngineState.reroutePinCommits` and `followBarrierViolations` say the new rule
(e1 §7 step 5's list).

The test changes, one to one (G3; these are WP-F's own tests, not pre-existing CDN tests, so `MIGRATION.md` takes no
entry):

- rr21-T8b (`EngineFollowBarrierRerouteRequeueTests.swift`): `owedReroutePinnedToARequeuedJobFollowsTheCopy`, "R-SYN-11:
  an owed re-route pinned to a job an ENOENT re-queued before the replay follows the copy then (F-28, T22)", becomes
  `owedReroutePinnedToARequeuedJobKeepsThePin`, "… before the replay keeps the pin, and X's commit re-routes it (F-28,
  D-13, T22)". The replay's assertion (cycle 21's `:124`) was `replayed.x == [xID] && replayed.w == ids` ("the replay
  follows K1's copy: W's job holds zz-a1…zz-a3, X only zz-x"); it is `replayed.x == (ids + [xID]).sorted() &&
  replayed.w.isEmpty` ("the pin holds: X holds zz-a1…zz-a3 and zz-x, and W has no job"). The serving loop (`:127`) went
  W then X; it goes X then W, since W's job appears only at X's commit, which re-routes W1…W3 under K1's copy. The answers
  are unchanged (K 16 bytes, V2 18, W1…W3 20), and the docs say the kept pin.
- The PIN-END invariants test (`invariantsReportCommitsKeptForOwedReroutes`, its name kept): its writes of the map are
  `PinEnd(serial:keepsEntry: false)`, and its three expected messages read "pin ends kept for owed re-routes" where they
  read "commits kept for owed re-routes", as the engine's do now.
- `enoentAfterCancelIsTheCancellation` (`EngineRaceTests.swift`, the D-13 test) reads `invariantViolations()` after the
  fresh attempt and expects none: the killer the ruling names for the write's `!eventsAfterFollow.isEmpty` forced true
  (a record kept with the barrier down). The test has no follow, so its orders are moot (must-fix 2).
- T-E2 and T-E5 (green on `d5b2ab9`, step 0) land with the fix.

On `5ad245d` (`.build-s3f/c22/e1r1-tests.log`): 23 tests in 2 suites passed, each in both orders (T-E1 in orders ×
owe): rr21-T8b as changed, T-E1 to T-E5, and the regression controls of 12.5.7 (the PIN-END suite's seven tests,
`FBJoinGapFailure`'s five, Shape A and probe (ii)'s four, and the D-13 test). e1-R1's kills are step 7's.

**The probes** (12.2; each asserts visit-first's answers and runs in every order that reaches it):

- **e1-PS: red, fixed.** `EngineFollowBarrierReroutePinSupersedeTests.swift` (`pinSuperseded`) is `pinEnd`'s shape with
  X's own publication superseded: K1 maps zz-a1…zz-a3 to W's content and zz-x off X's content (to X2's, 26 bytes) while
  X publishes, so the store refuses X's publication (the setup requires that it bound nothing). (i) K2 maps the pair to
  Z's content while W publishes, W's bytes failing their check; (ii) K2 drops the pair while W downloads, and K3 lists it
  again on Z's content. Visit-first: (i) W's integrity failure for W1…W3 (and U), (ii) `.notFound` for W1…W3; V gets
  X2's bytes, K O's, and Z is never requested. On `5ad245d` both were red in both orders (`34b299c`, the failing test
  alone; `.build-s3f/c22/e1-ps-red.log`): W1…W3 got Z's 24 bytes and Z was requested once; U, V and K got visit-first's
  answers. The fix (`b4eebb1`) is the ruling's route: the `.superseded` arm writes the commit-shaped record
  (`keepsEntry: false`) while events wait, before `supersede` (which may owe a batch of its own); the docs of `PinEnd`,
  `EngineState.reroutePinCommits`, `rerouteListing`, `followLayers` and `followBarrierViolations` name the supersede.
  On `b4eebb1` both e1-PS tests and the controls above passed in both orders (25 tests,
  `.build-s3f/c22/ps-fix-run.log`), and the Sync bundle passed whole: "Test run with 688 tests in 56 suites passed after
  354.368 seconds" (`.build-s3f/c22/ps-fix-sync.log`). Its branches' kills are step 7's (12.5.4).
- **e1-P1: red, fixed.** `EngineFollowBarrierReroutePinSpaceTests.swift` (`pinSpaceRead`) is `pinEnd`'s shape with X's
  publication failing ENOSPC at an interactive cap of one attempt: K0 maps zz-a1…zz-a3 to X's content, O's commit owes
  their re-routes, K1 maps them to W's content while X publishes (K1's layer pins X); X's placement rename then fails
  ENOSPC, and the free-space read that follows is held on the store's metadata executor while the follow's and the
  drain's turns run. Visit-first: O's commit re-routed W1…W3 onto X publishing, K1's visit passed X, and the ENOSPC's
  verdict answered V2 and W1…W3 with the space figures; X requested once, W never. A first form on `RacingSource` hung to
  the time limit (its cancel ends no stream, so a fresh attempt's 404 never came); the committed form runs on the
  scripted source, through `stageOwedCommit`'s and `setUpHeldPublications`' new `metadata:` parameter. On `b4eebb1` it
  was red in both orders (`94aa4b5`, the failing test alone; `.build-s3f/c22/e1-p1-red.log`): the drain's replay of the
  batch joined zz-a1 onto X (failed, its end recorded, its verdict not yet deferred), `relane`'s T20 re-queued X, so
  zz-a2 and zz-a3 found X off its end with no record and went to W by the engine's copy; X's fresh attempt got the 404
  ("X at the drain's end failed(untilEntryChanges) holding [zz-a1, zz-x] … W … holding [zz-a2, zz-a3]; X started 2
  times, W 1"), and V2 and W1…W3 got `.notFound`.

  The design. `relane`'s guard held for the follow's own visit (`inFollowVisit`, dated by the applies followed) and for
  a verdict already deferred, not for the drain's replays; e1 §3 names both the pin's replay and a user join. Options: (a)
  add the drain to the visit's clause with the same count of applies; (b) date the replayed event against the end. (a)
  is smaller but wrong on the other side: an event that arrived inside the read, with no apply since the end, would keep
  X failed where visit-first's request met X failed and re-queued it (T20, the verdict skipped). The clock cannot tell the
  two apart (many instants share one reading of it). Chosen: (b). Every stamp `worldStamp()` mints carries its place
  (`WorldStamp.serial`, `EngineState.stampsMinted`, never reset, so an end kept across barriers is read right), and
  `recordPublicationEnd` keeps the count at the end (`AttemptEnd.stamped`; `b83112c`, which nothing read yet).
  `metInItsAttempt(_:)` (`58e2c1c`): inside a visit, the count of applies as before; outside one, a reading with a serial
  at most `stamped`. Outside a visit only the drain's replays set a reading that can re-lane (`verdictAnswers`' reading
  computes an answer only), so the drain needs no flag of its own. The drain's visit after a verdict
  (`visitingAfterVerdict`) is left out: it stands for visits at the applies since that verdict, not for the verdict's
  arrival (e1-P2 probes it). `relane`'s doc and comment say the rule.

  The other cases (`9005651`, red on `b83112c` in both orders, `.build-s3f/c22/e1p1-red.log`): the bound,
  `userJoinFromJustBeforeAnENOSPCReplayedInItsReadGetsItsVerdict`, a user request V3 whose join is the last instant
  minted before X's end (the setup requires `stamped` to equal its serial), expects visit-first's ENOSPC answers for V2,
  V3 and W1…W3; the other side, `userJoinFromInsideAnENOSPCsReadSkipsItsVerdict`, V3's request made inside the held read,
  expects T20: X's fresh attempt serves V2 and V3 its 18 bytes, and its commit binds zz-x only, so W1…W3 follow K1's copy
  to W's 404; X starts twice, W once. Red, the bound failed as e1-P1 did, and the other side hit the 3-minute limit
  (W1 cancelled, W started twice). One-to-one test changes (WP-F's own tests): the two `WorldStamp(at:view:)` literals,
  `EngineFollowBarrierDeferBucketTests.swift:747` (now the entry's own serial) and `EngineFollowShutdownTests.swift:84`
  (serial 1), as the type gained a field.

  On `58e2c1c` the three tests pass in both orders, and the Sync bundle passed whole: "Test run with 691 tests in 56
  suites passed after 352.741 seconds" (`.build-s3f/c22/e1p1-sync.log`; load 3.65 4.51 4.06). The kills are step 7's:
  the rule false (e1-P1, the bound), true for any replay (the other side), `<=` as `<` (the bound), the end's count not
  kept (e1-P1).

  Residuals, not probed (UNCONFIRMED, reported): (1) a transfer's ENOSPC (`Job.transferSpaceEnd`) keeps no `stamped`,
  so the drain's replay inside its two awaits (the resume point's and the free-space read) of an event that arrived
  while the job downloaded still re-queues it (T20), where visit-first's input met it downloading. Probe shape:
  `barrierGivesATransferENOSPCsVerdictAtTheCapAfterTheFollowsJoinInItsRead` with a user join made behind the barrier
  before the transfer's ENOSPC and the drain released inside the read; visit-first, the ENOSPC's verdict at the cap.
  (2) The visit's clause dates a visit by the latest apply (cycle 21's count): a visit made after an apply that came
  since the end, of a job owed since an apply before it that mapped the id to X's content, re-queues X, where
  visit-first's visit at that earlier apply met X publishing. Reaching it needs an apply inside the read.
- **e1-P2: red, fixed.** `EngineFollowBarrierAfterVerdictSpaceTests.swift` (`afterVerdictSpaceRead`): X (zz-x, 18 bytes)
  and Y (zz-y, 20 bytes) download for the user waiters Vx and Vy at an interactive cap of one attempt, and X's
  publication is held at its first store unit; v3 makes the follow owe its visits; Y's attempt then ends in
  `.cancelled(.byClient)`, whose verdict is a re-queue (it answers nobody and counts nothing, so the cap of one attempt,
  which the ENOSPC's verdict needs to answer, does not answer Vy at Y's own verdict); K maps zz-y to X's content while X
  publishes (`beforeEnd`, the probe) or inside the held read (`inRead`, its other side); X's placement rename fails
  ENOSPC and the free-space read is held while the follow's and the drain's turns run. Swept first, K's visit passes Y,
  whose verdict waits, and the drain gives Y's verdict and its visit after it (`followAfterVerdict`) moves zz-y onto X.
  Visit-first: (probe) K's visit joined zz-y to X publishing, and the ENOSPC's verdict, at the cap, answered Vx and Vy
  with the space figures, X requested once; (other side) K's visit met X failed with its verdict to come and re-queued
  it (T20), and X's fresh attempt served both its 18 bytes. On `58e2c1c` the probe was red swept first
  (`f7c993f`, the failing test alone; `.build-s3f/c22/e1-p2-red.log`): "X at the drain's end downloading holding
  [zz-x, zz-y]; Vx failure(notFound), Vy failure(notFound); X started 2 times, Y 1": the visit after Y's verdict joined
  zz-y onto X failed in its read, T20 re-queued X, the ENOSPC's verdict was skipped, and X's fresh attempt got the 404.
  Visited first it gave visit-first's answers, and the other side passed in both orders.

  The design. `metInItsAttempt`'s visit branch reads `inFollowVisit || visitingAfterVerdict` (`75b9e45`), and the replay
  branch loses its `!visitingAfterVerdict` conjunct, which that branch now takes. Options: (a) the count of applies, as
  for the follow's visit; (b) the replay's instant. (b) is wrong: the visit's reading is the verdict's arrival, before
  X's end even when the apply that moved the id came after it, so the other side would keep X failed. (a) is the visit's
  own meaning: it makes the moves of the applies since the verdict deferred (`movesAfterVerdict`), which a visit-first
  engine made at those applies. `relane`'s comment says it. On `75b9e45` e1-P1's three tests, e1-P2's two, the
  space-read tests (`InItsRead`, three), `barrierSkipsTheBackoffForAVisitAfterAPublicationsEnd` and the later-verdict
  test (ten cases) pass in both orders (`.build-s3f/c22/p2-fix-run.log`, 9 tests), and the Sync bundle passed whole:
  "Test run with 693 tests in 56 suites passed after 357.153 seconds" (`.build-s3f/c22/e1p2-sync.log`; load 2.61 3.44
  3.74). The kills are step 7's: `|| visitingAfterVerdict` dropped (the probe), the replay's rule or `true` for that
  visit (the other side). Y's request count is recorded, not asserted: the re-queue's fresh attempt that visit-first
  made before K is not made behind the barrier (the red run read Y started once swept first). e1-P1's residual (2)
  applies to this visit as to the follow's.
- **e1-P3: holds** (`a83f54e`). Two sides, each in both orders, recording the job's state where it is read and
  asserting visit-first's answers only (no `#require` on the state). Shape A:
  `edgeBetweenAnENOENTRequeueAndTheOwedMoveKeepsTheVisitFirstAnswers` (`EngineFollowBarrierRequeueEdgeTests.swift`),
  `barrierMakesAMoveOntoAJobItsDrainedPublicationReQueued`'s setup with the network dropping and returning
  (`EngineRegressionCycle10Tests.offline`, then `DeviceConditions.unrestricted`) once T's drained publication fails
  ENOENT. rr21-T8b: `owedReroutePinnedToARequeuedJobKeepsThePin` gains an `edge` argument (its `false` case is the test
  as it was; one-to-one change: the arguments `LaneDropVisit.allCases` become `LaneDropVisit.allCases, [false, true]`,
  and the replay assertion's message carries X's state at the replay), whose drop and return come after K0 and before
  O's commit. A temporary print (removed before the commit; `.build-s3f/c22/e1-p3-probe.log`, `e1-p3-order.log`) read:
  Shape A swept first, "at the move T queued at epoch 8, move owed true, 2 events waiting" (the elements apply at once
  and their decisions about jobs wait for the drain, which comes after the follow's turns, so no replay can come
  between the re-queue and the move in this shape); visited first, T was already publishing its fresh attempt
  ("verifying at epoch 8, move owed false"); A and X got T's 100,000 bytes in both orders, T started twice. rr21-T8b
  swept first with the edge: the waiting events at X's re-queue were "[conditions(edge: false), conditions(edge:
  true), reroutes(…)]", so the drain replayed both elements' decisions between the re-queue and the batch, and X at
  the replay was "queued at epoch 6", the pin's epoch, in every case; the pin held (X held zz-a1…zz-a3 and zz-x) and
  the answers were rr21-T8b's (K 16, V2 18, W1…W3 20). No park at the same epoch: only the pump parks a queued job,
  and no pump runs behind the barrier, as e1 §3 read. The move's `.queued` arm keeps its dependency on that, now tested
  by these two cases. On `a83f54e` the two tests and Shape A's own pass (`.build-s3f/c22/e1-p3-run.log`).
- **e1-PR: holds** (`2b33c73`). `owedReroutePinnedToARequeuedJobDroppedBeforeTheReplayKeepsTheVisitFirstAnswers`
  (`EngineFollowBarrierRequeueRemovalTests.swift`, `sweepFollowsFirst` only, as the ruling says): rr21-T8b's setup with
  V2, X's only interest, withdrawn behind the barrier after K0 and before O's commit, so its removal waits ahead of the
  batch (the setup requires it first at X's re-queue). It was built at the first attempt. A temporary print (removed;
  `.build-s3f/c22/e1-pr-probe.log`) read: "X at the replay queued at epoch 6 holding [zz-x], after it downloading at
  epoch 8 holding [zz-a1, zz-a2, zz-a3] (pin epoch 6); X's content requested 2 times, W's 1": the drain turn that
